source_text: Si vero apud insanos furor insanabilis perseverarit, et, recedente Spiritu sancto, quae coepit caecitas in sua nocte permanserit, consilium nobis erit singulos fratres ab eorum fallacia separare, et, ne quis in laqueos erroris incurrat, ab eorum contagione secernere, quando nec oblatio sanctificari illic possit ubi Spiritus sanctus non sit, nec cuiquam Dominus per ejus orationes et preces prosit qui Dominum ipse violavit. Quod si Fortunatianus, aut immemor criminis sui per diaboli caecitatem, aut minister et servus diabol factus ad decipiendam fraternitatem, in hoc suo furore permanserit, vos quantum potestis elaborate, et in hac caligine diaboli saevientis fratrum mentes ab errore revocate, ne alienae dementiae facile consentiant, ne se desperatorum delictis participes faciant, sed teneant integri salutis suae et integritatis conservatae a se et custoditae perpetuum tenorem.
pass_a_gloss: But if indeed among the insane an incurable fury persists, and, with the Holy Spirit departing, the blindness that began remains in its own night, our plan will be to separate individual brothers from their deception, and to set them apart from their contagion, so that no one falls into the snares of error. For neither can an offering be sanctified there where the Holy Spirit is not, nor can the Lord benefit anyone through their prayers and supplications who has himself violated the Lord. If Fortunatianus, either having forgotten his own crime due to the devil's blindness or having become a minister and servant of the devil to deceive the brotherhood, persists in this his fury, you should strive as much as you can, and in this darkness of the raging devil, recall the minds of the brothers from error, so that they do not easily consent to alien madness, do not make themselves participants in the crimes of the desperate, but rather hold on to the perpetual continuity of their preserved and guarded salvation and integrity.

pass_b_english: But if an incurable fury persists among the insane, and the blindness that began remains in its own night after the Holy Spirit has departed, our plan will be to separate individual brothers from their deception and set them apart from their contagion so that no one falls into the snares of error. For an offering cannot be sanctified where the Holy Spirit is not, nor can the Lord benefit anyone through the prayers and supplications of one who has himself violated the Lord. If Fortunatianus persists in this fury of his, whether he has forgotten his own crime through the devil's blindness or has become a minister and servant of the devil to deceive the brotherhood, you must strive as much as you can. In this darkness of the raging devil, recall the minds of the brothers from error so that they do not easily consent to alien madness or make themselves participants in the crimes of the desperate, but rather hold fast to the perpetual continuity of their salvation and integrity, which they have preserved and guarded.
